quizzes.title: Module Intro: Before You Begin
quizzes.description: Welcome to this module. This short survey is not graded for correctness. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting.

questions.text: What helps a large country feel like one people, and what can pull it apart? Give your best answer now. You will come back to this question at the end of the module.

This module has these goals. Read them, then choose one answer.

  • Explain how radio, movies, and national heroes created a shared American culture in the 1920s.
  • Describe the contribution of Black artists to jazz and the Harlem Renaissance.
  • Evaluate whether a shared mass culture can bind citizens together as a political community.
  • Explain why Prohibition failed to win lasting public support and what that suggests about law and civic habits.
  • Describe the Klan, the Scopes Trial, and Marcus Garvey's movement as responses to a changing America.
  • Evaluate whether the 1920s are better described as a Jazz Age or a culture war.

questions.text: What is still unclear to you? Name a person, event, or idea. If nothing is unclear, write "nothing."
Which of these did the people in this module most need, whether they had it or not?

Pick one person from this module (Lindbergh, Hughes, Bryan, Darrow, Garvey, or someone else) and explain, in two or three sentences, how that virtue showed up in what they did, or how its absence did.

discussions.title: Discussion: Jazz Age or Culture War: Which Was the Real 1920s?
discussions.html:
Was the real 1920s the Jazz Age of radio, movies, and new music, or the culture war over Prohibition, the Klan, the Scopes Trial, and who counted as a "real American"? The lessons ask you to decide.

Your post (about 100 to 150 words):

  1. Take a clear position: Jazz Age, culture war, or both about equally.
  2. Give one specific piece of evidence from this week's lessons that supports you.
  3. Name one fact that cuts against your position, and explain why you still hold it.

Your reply (about 50 to 75 words): Respond to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with something they did not use. If not, say respectfully where their reasoning falls short.

Post first, then reply.
